applied_by: scripts/tuam_studio.py, from scripts/build_candidate.py (the release only; the Study 3 fonts stay as traced); edits run in order
frame: font units, after Font2.zones: baseline 0, x from the glyph's left edge before spacing

accent_gap.why: the gap under every accent, the builder's 19 (0.035 x-height) raised to the 26 to 38 units N45 prints under the fadas of é, í, ó and ú

crossbar_at.why: đ and ð: the bar 0.48 of the way up the ascender from the x-height (the builder 0.42), so ð's slanted bar stays clear of d's raised bowl and its slit stays open

upper_clearance.why: above the x-height every pair is kerned at least a cut's width apart: f's flag came within 10 units of the next ascender (fl, fb, fh, fk) and of a fada

italic_condense.why: the Italic narrowed (0.96) and given back the weight the first pass's plain narrowing had lost (stems 210 to 213 against the Regular's 220, o 207 against 216): every edge moved out 4.4 units across by the drawing's own nodes (not the builder's stroked offset, which drew the curves in short pieces), then each cut, slit and seam narrower than 45 put back, as the slope will show it, to its width before the growth by the side that ends there (a spur drawn back along the gap; the right-hand strokes of v and w moved over; half each where the sides are alike); an accented letter is its letter as grown, its marks grown on their own; the few glyphs whose hairline gaps the growth would close (eth, the fractions one half and one quarter, the trade mark, the braces) keep the narrowing alone; nodes added where the sloped curves pass their extremes

italic_settle.why: after the slant every Italic outline settled on the unit grid (scripts/settle.py, as Carrick's, pieces under 8 units folded, repeated until it changes nothing): rounding the sloped curves had left 194 joins bent 3 to 25 degrees and 62 pieces under 8 units in the 41 traced letters, figures and signs (the Regular has 76 and 17); now 72 and 8

iacute_rise.why: the acute of i drawn steeper, its right end raised 100 units over its width (a vertical shear about its thin left end: 223 x 125 at 19 degrees to 223 x 213 at 40), so that i and its accented form are told apart at 14 to 20 px; the prints already set it steeper and taller than the dot (N45: 18 degrees and 136 units against the dot's 3 degrees and 74; the production sheet 13 to 14 degrees against 1 to 3), but at text sizes the traced acute and the 249 x 93 dot rendered alike; its width, its thin left end, its place right of the stem and its gap (30, closer than the dot's 40, as the prints set it) are kept; of the options proofed (the shared acute of a, e, o, u; the gap raised; the acute taller, rotated or less steep) it is the least change that passes the legibility check at every size, and it still reads as a fada, not a raised dot

comma.why: the comma, and with it the quotes, the apostrophe, the semicolon and the marks made from the comma, with a heavier tail: its inner side moved out (where it leaves the dot 0.45 to 0.30 of the dot's width, its inner corner 0.42 to 0.25), its tip and outer corner kept, so it is the same wedge, about 120 thick (the review's skeleton measure 84 to 123) against stems of 220; its outer side now leaves the dot at the dot's right extreme, where the builder's tail began below the dot and left a notch; no print sets a comma or quote (N45, N46 and the production sheet print none; Hayes's 1974 cover lettering, Bolger fig. 204, has an apostrophe drawn as a short flat dash of the dot's weight)

straight_quotes.why: third pass: the straight quote and double quote were the builder's wedge at the size the face's first period gave it (160 by 116 units, its skeleton weight 82 against the curly quotes' and apostrophe's 123), so they set grey beside them; the wedge is scaled by 1.53 about the middle of its top, its taper and proportions kept and its top on the quotes' line, to the curly quotes' weight (124, median 86 against 92); the primes, made from it, follow

ponc.why: the ponc on the ascender letters stood 30 units above the stem and merged with it at 14 px: on b and d it is set beside the ascender over the bowl, as Hayes letters the dotted b of leabhair in this face on his 1974 cover (Bolger fig. 204: the dot over the bowl's counter, centred on the height of the ascender above the x-height), so centred over the counter and on that height (61 above the bowl), at least 70 from the ascender (60 in the Italic, after its growth); f has no bowl and its flag fills the space right of its stem, so its dot stays above the stem, 60 clear of it (the line's ascender rises from 934 to 951 to hold it); the mark feature's anchors on b, d and f follow

word_space.why: fourth pass: the word space half the n, the rule the builder sets every face's space by, without its 320-unit cap (build2.Font2.space), which held Tuam's to 0.36 of its 897-unit n and to 2.2 times n's sidebearings (3.0 to 6.7 in the other faces), so that short Irish words (a, an, ar, na, i) ran into their neighbours at every size; 448 (the Italic's 435, from its 870 n), the no-break space with it: of 320, 380, 400, 420, 448 and 470 set in Irish and English at 14 to 28 px and 48 px, 400 and over part the words at 14 to 16 px where 320 does not; 448 is the family's rule and the most that opens no holes (470 does, at 14 and 28 px), generous but even at 48 px, and its word white (space plus the letters' sidebearings, 568 on average) is 4.9 times the white between letters (Tuam's round letters set wide), still the least in the family (5.7 to 9.2), so it is not loose for the face

edits.why: spur and hook ends drawn as one sharp point: the traces end them in spikes, flats and blunt ends that no print resolves
o printed as tall as n and c on both prints; the builder's baseline snap left it 14 units short, past zones' tolerance
l as tall as b, d, h, k on N46; 15 units short
9 sits on the line at the height of 8 and 0 on both prints; the trace was 21 units short and snapped as round
? and ! at the figures' height on both prints, their dots on the baseline as the period's
flat tops on the x-height: the traces' tops run 529 to 543 with arches and bowls printed low; each top is lifted whole, its stroke's thickness kept
bowls of p, q and y on the baseline, as every other bowl
i and j stems to the x-height, as on both prints; their dots go up with them
vertical stems evened to 220, the face's median: N45 prints them 211 to 222, the traces 213 to 228 (N46's blur thickens some); each edge moves half the difference
stray nodes merged into the corners they blur: the beaks of r and u, the foot of b, the crotches of p and g (sharp, as q has it), the eye of e, the foot of l
the inner turn of s drawn as one curve, not three facets
the arch cuts at one width: N45 prints n, m, h, u and f at 25 to 29 units (the traces 23 to 37); r and y as the rest
each slit as wide as N45, the clean print, measures it on the same raster (b, o, p and 0 had drifted 6 to 14 units from it in tracing); the widths stated are geometric, about 3 over that measure
the vertex seams of v and w at N45's 14 to 17 units: averaging with N46, which fills them, had halved them to 8 to 12
5's flag cut at N45's 21 units (the mean of the prints had narrowed it to 13)
the dots 40 units from their strokes: N45 prints them 37 to 45 apart, the mean with N46 (18 to 26) had closed them to 25 to 32; j takes i's dot and ? takes !'s, as one dot each
r's top on the x-height with the arches of n, m and h (544): its arm's flat top was 2 units low (542), the one arch the first pass did not level

derived_frame: font units, x from the glyph's own left edge (narrowed by 0.96 in the Italic, which has them before its narrowing); the upright has them after spacing

derived.why: the joins of the two s that make the section sign drawn as continuous curves, with no piece under 8 units: the lower counter's tip, where lightening the s left five pieces of 1 to 9 units
the left side below the notch where the two s meet, which turned 76 degrees on pieces of 2 to 8 units, one curve from the corner of the lower s's top down to the side
the rounded corners at the foot of each s, two pieces of 5 and 7 units, one curve
then the whole outline settled (settled(), as the Italic is): the joins of the s it is made from that bend 3 to 8 degrees made smooth

fifth_pass.about: A fourth independent review of the released fonts (font outlines only) found three defects shared by the four faces. Each is corrected by one rule for all of them, in scripts/symbols.py (approx_sign, ring_weight, ring_letters, heavier_ring) and scripts/build2.py (Font2.stack_anchors, bottom_clear, the mark and mkmk features), switched on for the release by scripts/build_candidate.py (APPROX_WHITE, RING_SHARE, MARK_STACKS); the study fonts do not change. Measurements are font units, from the fonts before and after.

approxequal.why: ≈ stood 466 tall (23..489) against the ='s 365 (73..438), its waves 99 heavy against bars of 112 and 155 apart against the ='s 143; its waves are now drawn at the bars' weight (109, Italic 110), centred on the bars on the 255.5 axis, 0.7 of the ='s white apart (101, Italic 98): 425 tall (43..468)

rings.why: the rings of © ® @ ° ¤ were 50 to 77 beside an o of 216; each is now at least half of it, 110 (Italic 109 to 115), © and ® grown outward (690 to 773 tall, Italic 784) and @ (807 to 839) with their letters as drawn, 31 to 35 from the ring; ° has a counter of 77 (63 before), ¤ one of 165 (237)

marks.why: the ponc construction (constructions, ponc) sets the dot of ḃ and ḋ beside the ascender and ḟ's 60 above its stem, and the ponc's anchor was the only top anchor, so every top mark followed it: a dieresis on b or d stood 64 and 58 into the ascender, and any mark stood 60 over f where it stands 30 over h k l; no mkmk (176 into each other), no anchor on a precomposed letter, the comma below ran through f's and j's descenders (155 into them), and U+0323 had no glyph; now top marks stand the face's accent gap of 30 clear, as the precomposed accents do, on every letter, stacks 30 apart, comma and dot below at least 30 clear; one rule in every face: the dot above (U+0307) keeps the anchor the ponc is set by, so ḃ ċ ḋ ḟ ġ ṁ ṗ ṡ ṫ and every base + U+0307 shape exactly as before; every other top mark takes the place the face's accents take on its letters (not the ponc's), raised where the letter's own ink comes closer than the face's accent gap (the white of the precomposed vowels); each precomposed letter carries top, ponc and bottom anchors of its own, so a mark typed after it stands on its accent; an mkmk feature sets a second mark above (or below) the first, the same gap apart; a comma or dot below moves along the line, then down, until it stands clear of a descender; U+0323 (combining dot below) is added, the face's dot

changed.why: every glyph whose outline differs from the fourth pass's fonts, per style (with the added dotbelowcomb); kerning changes only in pairs with one of them, the builder's own method applied to the new shapes; the line box, names and every other outline are unchanged
